instructions: Put 3 of the eggs in a small pot, cover them with cold water and bring it to a boil over high heat. Turn the heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes, then move the eggs into a bowl of cold water.

Meanwhile, start the dough. Stir 2 cups of the flour and 1/2 tsp of the salt together in a big bowl. Pour in the 1/4 cup olive oil and 1/2 cup water and stir with a fork until it comes together in a shaggy ball.
Transfer it onto the counter and knead for about 5 minutes, until it's smooth and soft. Turn the bowl upside down over it and leave it to rest for 30 minutes.
While the dough rests, finely dice the onion and the red pepper, and mince the 2 garlic cloves.
Drain the 3 cans of tuna through a sieve set over a bowl, and keep the oil. Put 3 tbsp of the tuna oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the onion, the pepper and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt. Cook for about 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until they're soft and sweet but not brown.

Add the garlic and the 1/2 tsp smoked paprika and stir for 30 seconds, until it smells toasty. Stir in 1/2 cup passata and let it bubble for 3 to 4 minutes, until it's thick enough that a spoon leaves a trail across the pan.

Take the pan off the heat. Flake in the tuna, add the 1/4 tsp pepper and stir. Taste it, and add a pinch more salt if it's flat. Spread it out on a plate to cool. A warm filling makes the bottom crust soggy.
Heat the oven to 375°F and line a baking sheet with parchment. Peel the 3 cooked eggs and slice them into rounds.

Dust the counter with the last 1/4 cup of flour. Cut the dough into two pieces, one a little bigger than the other. Roll the bigger piece into a rectangle about 10 by 13 inches, as thin as you can get it, and lay it on the sheet.
Spread the cooled filling over the dough, leaving a 1 inch border all the way round. Lay the egg slices over the filling.
Roll the smaller piece of dough into a rectangle about 9 by 12 inches and lay it over the top. Fold the bottom edge up over the top edge and pinch it closed all the way round.
Beat the last egg and brush it all over the top. Cut a small hole in the middle with a knife for the steam.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until the top is deep golden and the crust sounds hollow when you tap it.
Let it cool on the sheet for at least 20 minutes, then cut it into squares. It slices most neatly at room temperature.
Serve it warm or at room temperature, or wrap the cooled squares for packed lunches.
method_notes: All three versions fill a thin two-crust pie with onion and pepper cooked slowly in olive oil, tomato and drained tuna, then glaze it with beaten egg and bake it on a flat sheet. Spain on a Fork uses an unyeasted dough of flour, olive oil and water, cooks the vegetables in the oil from the tuna cans, and lays sliced hard-boiled eggs over the filling. Caroline's Cooking and Recipes From Europe use a yeasted dough, with Recipes From Europe adding garlic and using far more onion, and Caroline's adding white wine to the dough. This one follows Spain on a Fork with one whole red pepper in place of two half peppers and a little garlic from Recipes From Europe. No version had 20 or more ratings and RecipeTin Eats (the trusted cook for Spanish) has no version, so the first read version leads.
